Bridge span structure (English: superstructure) is also called superstructure
It is the main load-bearing structure that crosses obstacles when the line is interrupted.
It includes the bridge deck.
Bridge deck beams and the structural components that support them
Such as main beams (slabs)
arch
Suspension cables, etc.
Its function is to bear the load generated by pedestrians and vehicles on the bridge.
The span is relatively large
In addition to the requirement of safely withstanding large vehicle loads, the load must also be constant.
The construction of bridge span structures is therefore relatively complex.
Construction is also quite difficult.
Bearings are important structural components that connect the superstructure and substructure of a bridge.
It can reliably transfer the reaction force of the bridge superstructure to the bridge substructure.
And ensure that the bridge span structure can generate sufficient deformation (including displacement and rotation).
This ensures that the actual stress condition of the structure matches the calculated theoretical diagram.
Piers and abutments (also known as substructure)
It is the supporting structure of the bridge span and the load-bearing capacity of dead and live loads.
This live load includes loads such as vehicles and pedestrians.
Buildings transferred to the foundation
The structures typically located at both ends of a bridge are called abutments.
Bridge abutments connect with road embankments
To resist the horizontal earth pressure of the embankment
Preventing landslides and collapses of embankment fill
The one placed in the middle of the span is called a bridge pier.
Single-span bridges do not have intermediate piers.
The bottom structural part of the bridge piers and abutments that transfers all loads to the foundation.
It is usually referred to as the foundation.
It is key to ensuring the safe use of bridges.
Because foundations are often buried deep in the soil.
And sometimes underwater construction is required.
Therefore, it is also one of the more difficult parts of bridge construction.
